prayerExcerpt.en-US: Water quencheth a flaming fire, and alms resisteth sin.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: A água apaga o fogo abrasador, e a esmola resiste ao pecado.

meta.face: A Carthaginian of Roman Africa of about sixty-five, with a warm olive-brown complexion and a LONG face with DEEPLY SUNKEN TEMPLES and a TALL, ROUNDED crown; a strongly ARCHED, bony nose, LARGE, gentle dark eyes under HEAVY LIDS, thick, curved black-grey brows, full lips in a WIDE, generous mouth, a short, TIGHTLY CURLED white beard close along the jaw, close-cropped curly white hair; the gaze turned kindly toward the poor man.
meta.basis: No likeness survives; the Milanese statue on his Wikipedia page is a generic mitred bishop. The book tells a citizen of Carthage chosen bishop in 481, charitable to excess, twice exiled by the Vandal kings, who died near Albi in 505. The card shows the alms of his Reflection; the face is ours.
